newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma seeks renewed trade with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma seeks renewed trade with Iraq.

text.p: Russia's lower house of parliament on Wednesday passed by an overwhelming majority a law seeking a renewal of trade between Russia and Iraq, calling on Moscow to ignore international sanctions against Baghdad.

The non-binding law would re-establish trade ties, allow Russia to buy Iraqi oil and allow for Russian machinery sales and humanitarian aid to Baghdad. It was put forward by the Duma's ultra-nationalist group, headed by Vladimir Zhirinovsky.

Foreign ministry officials were not available for comment. Officials have said they are keen to boost trade with Iraq, but that they will respect U.N. sanctions, imposed in August 1990 when Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait.
The U.N. Security Council has since allowed a six-month oil-for-food deal allowing $2 billion worth of oil sales over six months so Baghdad can buy food and medicine.
Russian firms fought hard to get the oil purchase contracts late last year under the U.N. Security Council auspices.
